job_description.title: Senior Backend Engineer
job_description.raw_text:
Senior Backend Engineer — CloudCore (Remote)

CloudCore builds the control plane for multi-cloud deployments. We are hiring a Senior Backend Engineer to own core platform services.

What you will do:
- Design and operate high-availability APIs consumed by thousands of engineering teams
- Own PostgreSQL schema design and query performance for the platform's metadata store
- Evolve our GraphQL gateway that fronts internal service APIs
- Run workloads on Kubernetes and manage infrastructure with Terraform

Requirements:
- 4+ years building backend services in Python
- Deep experience designing and versioning REST APIs
- Production PostgreSQL experience, including performance tuning
- Hands-on Kubernetes experience (deployment, scaling, debugging)
- Experience with GraphQL schema design and federation
- Infrastructure-as-code experience with Terraform

interview_questions.question: Your REST platform at Finlytics serves 2.3M requests/day at a p95 under 180ms. Walk me through how you'd diagnose a sudden p95 regression to 500ms — what do you look at first and why?
You reduced PostgreSQL query latency by 45% through index and pooling changes. How do you decide when an index helps versus when it hurts write-heavy tables like a payments ledger?
LedgerLite implements double-entry bookkeeping in FastAPI. How did you enforce transactional integrity across accounts, and what would break first under concurrent postings?
You moved payment reconciliation to Celery-based event-driven workers. How did you handle idempotency and poison messages, and what monitoring told you the migration was safe?
Tell me about leading the 3-engineer reconciliation migration at Finlytics. How did you split the work, and what did you do when the timeline slipped?
Describe a time at CredWise when an automation you built (like the CI/CD pipeline) broke something downstream. How did you handle the fallout and what changed afterward?
Your open-source project has 14 external contributors. Tell me about a disagreement with a contributor over design direction and how you resolved it.

This role runs everything on Kubernetes, which isn't on your resume. How have you approached closing an infrastructure gap like this before, and what's your 90-day plan to get production-safe with it?
CloudCore fronts internal APIs with a GraphQL gateway. Given your REST-first background, how would you evaluate what belongs in the graph versus staying REST, and where would you expect friction?

At Finlytics I own a REST platform doing 2.3M requests a day, cut database latency 45%, and led the move to event-driven reconciliation that turned a 6-hour batch into a 40-minute pipeline. I care about API contracts, boring reliability, and shipping.
about.detailed: I'm a backend engineer who likes owning services end to end — schema design, API contracts, deployment, and the 2am pager that keeps you honest. At Finlytics I run a REST API platform serving 2.3M requests a day at a p95 under 180ms, and I led three engineers through migrating payment reconciliation to event-driven Celery workers, cutting settlement from 6 hours to 40 minutes. Before that, at CredWise, I built KYC microservices handling 50,000 daily checks and automated the release pipeline down 70%. Outside work I maintain LedgerLite, an open-source double-entry bookkeeping API with 1,200 GitHub stars and 14 contributors. I'm happiest where correctness, throughput, and clean interfaces all matter at once.

job_description.title: Product Data Analyst
job_description.raw_text:
Product Data Analyst — Metricly (Hybrid, Pune)

Metricly is a product analytics platform. We're hiring a Product Data Analyst to own experiment analysis and self-serve reporting for our customers' product teams.

What you will do:
- Model product event data with dbt into clean, documented marts
- Build and maintain Power BI dashboards for customer-facing reporting
- Design and analyze A/B tests with our data science team

Requirements:
- Advanced SQL for analytics across large event datasets
- Python for data wrangling and statistical analysis
- Tableau experience for internal dashboarding
- Power BI experience for customer-facing report packs
- dbt experience for analytics engineering and data modeling

interview_questions.question: You analyzed churn across 800,000 records in SQL. Walk me through how you'd structure a cohort retention query, and how you'd keep it fast as the events table grows 10x.
Your checkout A/B tests lifted conversion 12% across 2M sessions. How did you determine sample size and guard against peeking, and when would you have called the test inconclusive?
In CartLens you modeled cart-abandonment drivers on 1.2M events. Which features mattered most, and how did you validate you weren't just modeling seasonality?
Your Tableau dashboard replaced 6 ad-hoc reports used by 40+ stakeholders. Tell me about a stakeholder who resisted giving up their spreadsheet — how did you win them over?
Describe a time your analysis contradicted what a product leader wanted to hear. What did you do, and what happened?
You automated attribution reporting from 10 hours to 45 minutes. What broke in the first month of automation, and how did you make it trustworthy?
This role models data with dbt, which you haven't used. Given your Python pipeline experience, how would you approach learning dbt's testing and documentation workflow in your first month?
Metricly's customer reporting runs on Power BI rather than Tableau. What do you expect to transfer directly, and what would you deliberately relearn?
